audit_wave6: Wave 6 audit: Gate F failed on measurement after shipping. An isolated reader holding only the pack and prompt.txt filed Tibu at 92.2 per 100,000 on 137 action-days, the shipped call with its rate and window count, at about 75 per cent confidence. It found the coverage correction unaided from the data: delivered items rose six to seven times from 1 April 2026 in three cities that each gained two new sources, while Tibu's feed was unchanged at 1.00 times against a 2.4 times rise in recorded actions. It named Sardinata as the trap and rejected it. Separate finding for whoever repairs this: the protocol never defines the measure of the rise, and a literal raw-count reading gives Sardinata, so the ranking measure is open on the shipped text. The build stays SHIPPED and pending portal review; this is pre-emptive evidence, not a portal result.

leak.reader: LANDED THE CALL at Tibu, 137 action-days, 92.2 per 100,000, but at about 45 to 50 per cent confidence with Sardinata at 121.4 named as the main alternative, and it says in terms that the pack never says which way to go. Question 1 clean, nothing names the decisive step, and it found no single-use file. Three findings to fix, and the first is the one that matters most. (1) ANNOUNCEMENT: protocol 4.1 reads "Los registros del Observatorio son la evidencia de esa actividad y no su medida", which the reader calls an unusual sentence for a working protocol. It is the build's whole thesis stated in the pack, which is leak-check sweep 5, and it is the shape that cost task196 a reader landing. Cut or reduce it to a clause that does not name the distinction. The Boletin's two cautions ("su cobertura no es uniforme entre municipios" and "no compara municipios entre si ni anticipa la designacion") and the dictionary's "Ninguno de los dos entra en el registro", which does the analyst's decoy sorting for them, are the same class and want the same treatment. (2) UNIFORMITY, the rule firing on the device itself: the April step is in exactly the three cities, and their new outlets send 40 to 76 items per row in a tight band against 5 to 10 everywhere else, which the reader says looks built to a step-change pattern rather than like the organic variation in the other 20 municipalities. Give the new outlets the per-row spread the existing ones have. (3) A date inconsistency: the dictionary is dated 5 November 2026 and the extract described as taken that day, while 2026 fecha_registro runs only to 2026-10-19. AND THE ONE TO WEIGH AGAINST THE JUDGE: the reader reports that only about 12 of Sardinata's 177 semester action-days are cited solely by the new outlets, so 165 of 177 survive dropping them, and that the old outlets' own volume also tripled. Its conclusion is that the three cities may carry a genuine surge too and the pack cannot separate the two. If that holds it is a Gate C finding rather than a Gate F one, because the decisive step would not be forced by the records. HOLD the fix pass for the judge, which is still running, and fix both sets in one generator pass.

reader_findings.measured_and_confirmed: the citation sources really are drawn close to independently of the delivery log, and this one has no date join in it. 23.0 per cent of the 12,544 mapped cita rows carry a source that ever remitted from that municipality, against a chance baseline near 20 per cent (median 8 sources per municipality out of 40 distinct in envios; citas draw from 21, 20 of them shared). reader_findings.measured_and_corrected: it reported the citation file clean for 2024 and broken only for 2025. Measured: 2024 carries 848 uncited entries and 643 orphan cite rows over 309 ids, 2025 carries 814 and 622 over 303, and 2026 alone is complete at 0 and 0. So it is a two-regime pattern, 2024 and 2025 partial against 2026 complete, with an ordinary migration story available. The repair is to qualify the dictionary line that overstates the cardinality ("una cita: un item que el registro vinculo a una entrada"), not to rebuild a year.
reader_findings.measured_and_dismissed: its most serious finding does not exist. It reported 2,587 of 6,773 day-municipality pairs citing more items than the filter retained, an impossibility, and I reproduced it at 2,740 of 22,075 with my own join. Both joins matched the citation publication date to the delivery log send date, which are different events. At municipality totals over the whole window, the one commensurable grain, cited runs at 40 to 70 per cent of retained and NO municipality exceeds it. Filed as a rule in dataset-generation. Do not repair this.
